column1: # THE EIGHTH SPELLING, AND THE DIRECTORY PRINTED IT ITSELF.
# LEIPHOLZ — with a P. Found on 20 September 2026 in the Berliner Adressbuch's own cross-reference,
# and swept the same day through the instruments that had never seen it.
field
column2: value

column1: the directory says so, in both directions
column2: the 1913 and 1924 volumes print "LEIPHOLZ, s. a. LEIBHOLZ" — see also. THE 1940 VOLUME PRINTS IT THE OTHER WAY ROUND: "LEIBHOLZ s. o. LEIPHOLZ". The compiler treated the two as one name for at least twenty-seven years, and by 1940 was pointing from ours to the other.

column1: why that matters more than a variant usually does
column2: THIS IS NOT A GUESS AT A MISSPELLING. It is the contemporary index-maker of the city these people lived in declaring that a reader looking for one should look at the other. Every bounded negative this archive has recorded for LEIBHOLZ, LAIBHOLZ, LEIBHOLTZ and LEIBBHOLZ was one spelling short of complete, and had been since the first of them was written down.

column1: # ---------------- IT IS A REAL BERLIN SURNAME, IN EVERY VOLUME SAMPLED ----------------
the counts
column2: pages carrying LEIPHOLZ in the Berliner Adressbuch: 1913 — 3 · 1920 — 1 · 1925 — 4 · 1930 — 4 · 1935 — 4 · 1938 — 4 · 1940 — 6 · 1943 — 4. Present in every volume tested across thirty years.

column1: who they were, from the 1924 run
column2: ERNST, Kaufmann, Spandau, Freiheit 4-7 · ADOLF, Polizei-Wachtmeister, NO18 Friedenstraße 30 · PAUL, Schlosser, S59 Dieffenbachstraße 58 · LUISE née PREJAWA, widow of an Amtsgerichts-Sekretär.

column1: *** AND ONE MAN MAY BE PRINTED UNDER BOTH SPELLINGS ***
column2: the 1924 Leipholz run has "ADOLF, POL. WACHTMSTR., NO18 FRIEDENSTR. 30". The 1940 LEIBHOLZ run — the one this archive has already published, the eleven householders — has "ADOLF, POL. BEAMT., NO18 FRIEDENSTR. 47". SAME FORENAME, SAME FORCE, SAME STREET, SAME POSTAL DISTRICT, sixteen years apart and seventeen house numbers along.

column1: what that would mean
column2: that the two spellings are not two families but one name written two ways by the same publisher — which is what the cross-reference says in words and what this would show in a person.

column1: *** AND IT IS NOT VERIFIED AT THE IMAGE, WHICH IS THIS ARCHIVE'S STANDARD ***
column2: both readings are from the TEXT LAYER ONLY. Three attempts were made to crop the 1924 page at the Leipholz run and all three returned a different column — the ALTO coordinates for that page do not map onto the served image the way they do elsewhere in the same series, and rather than crop blindly until something fits, the reading is published as what it is. A TEXT-LAYER HIT IS NOT A READ ENTRY. This archive said that this morning about a different page and it applies here.

column1: *** AND HER RECORD, OPENED 21 SEPTEMBER: NEUSTETTIN, AND SHE GOT OUT ***
column2: ELISABETH WEILER NÉE LEIPHOLZ, born 1 JANUARY 1891 at NEUSTETTIN in POMERANIA — Szczecinek today. Residence Berlin. Basis of persecution: racial. *** EMIGRATION: PALESTINE. *** She is in the Bundesarchiv's Residents' List (ID 1166673) and NOT in the Gedenkbuch, and now it is clear why: she survived. A caution on the date — 1 January is the commonest placeholder in these lists for a year known without a day, and it should not be read as a birthday.

column1: and Neustettin is the same belt again
column2: Neustettin sits among Tämpelburg, Zettin and Bärwalde, which are three of the Gedenkbuch's fifty birthplaces, and about sixty kilometres from Hammerstein where Sally Leibholz was born. A FOURTH INDEPENDENT POINT IN THE SAME CORNER OF POMERANIA, and the first one attached to a person who lived.

column1: *** MAPPING THE LIVES — ONE PERSON, AND SHE IS NEW ***
column2: searching the surname field for LEIPHOLZ returns exactly "1 persons": *** WEILER, ELISABETH NÉE LEIPHOLZ, BORN 1 JANUARY 1891, BERLIN. *** The database matches maiden names, which is how she surfaces. She is not in this archive under any spelling and was not in the 114 LEIBHOLZ persons the archive harvested from the same database earlier today. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD — a Berlin woman of the right generation with the eighth spelling of the name, and the first person the rule has actually produced.

column1: and the control was run on the same screen
column2: LEIBHOLZ returns the full hundred-capped list the archive already holds — Abrahamsohn née Leibholz, Alexander née Leibholz of Willmanndamm 6, Agnes née Kerger of Leinestraße 32, Alfred of Levetzowstraße 13 and the rest. THE HARNESS FINDS LEIBHOLZ AND FINDS ONE LEIPHOLZ. The single result is a result, not a failure to search.

column1: and one thing the control incidentally confirmed
column2: AGNES LEIBHOLZ NÉE KERGER, born 10 March 1889, Leinestraße 32 III rechts, Neukölln. This archive knew an Agnes Leibholz at Mehringdamm 109 from 1957 to 1976 and a Heinrich Leibholz, Verwaltungsbeamter, at Leinestraße 32 in Neukölln to 1942. THE ADDRESS MATCHES AND SHE NOW HAS A MAIDEN NAME AND A BIRTH DATE.

column1: *** YAD VASHEM — TWO PEOPLE, AND THEY PROVE THE WHOLE RULE ***
column2: the Shoah Names Database returns 7 results for LEIPHOLZ. Five are LIPHOLTZ of Kolno in Poland, a soundex match and a different family. THE OTHER TWO ARE BERLINERS, BOTH MURDERED, BOTH WITH A PAGE OF TESTIMONY: *** WILLI LEIPHOLZ, born 1887, Berlin *** and *** JENNY LEIPHOLZ, born 1893, Berlin. ***

column1: *** AND THE BUNDESARCHIV HAS THE SAME TWO PEOPLE SPELT WITH A B ***
column2: the fifty-name Gedenkbuch list read the same evening contains "LEIBHOLZ, WILHELM WILLI (* 30.12.1887 in Berlin)" and "LEIBHOLZ, JENNY (* 11.02.1893 in Loosen)". Same forenames, same birth years, same city. Yad Vashem's column is PLACE OF RESIDENCE, which is why it says Berlin for a woman born at Loosen.

column1: so the two spellings are one family, demonstrated on named people
column2: THE BERLINER ADRESSBUCH SAID SO IN WORDS — "Leipholz, s. a. Leibholz" — and this shows it on two individuals across two independent databases compiled by different institutions from different sources. A GERMAN FEDERAL ARCHIVE WROTE LEIBHOLZ AND A JERUSALEM MEMORIAL WROTE LEIPHOLZ ABOUT THE SAME MURDERED COUPLE. Every negative this archive has ever recorded under one spelling is provisional until it is run under the other.

column1: and it supersedes the weaker version of the same point
column2: this file earlier offered ADOLF the policeman of Friedenstraße as a man printed under both spellings, from the text layer, unverified at the image. That remains unverified and is now unnecessary. WILLI AND JENNY ARE THE PROOF, and they are read from two rendered result pages rather than from OCR.

column1: what to do with them
column2: a PAGE OF TESTIMONY names the SUBMITTER — a survivor or a relative who filled in the form, with their own address and their relationship to the dead. Two Pages of Testimony for a Berlin couple of exactly Jacob's generation. NOT KIN ON ANY EVIDENCE HELD. The pages are free to open and have not been.

column1: # ---------------- 6. GENETEKA, AND THE OPPOSITE WARNING ----------------
*** AND THE SILENT-FALLBACK TRAP CAUGHT THIS ARCHIVE A SECOND TIME ***
column2: LEIPHOLZ and LEIBHOLZ were first run with the province and record-type parameters left EMPTY. Both returned an empty table, and both were nearly written down as zeroes. THE CONTROL — Kowalski, with bdm=B and w=02kp filled in — returned rows immediately. An empty parameter does not mean "all provinces"; it means no result. The archive documented this fault on 20 September in the form of a wrong province code and met it again the same evening in the form of a missing one.

column1: *** RE-RUN PROPERLY: LEIPHOLZ FINDS WHAT LEIBHOLZ CANNOT, IN OUR OWN PROVINCE ***
column2: KUJAWSKO-POMORSKIE, births: LEIBHOLZ returns "Brak danych" — no data, 0 of 0. LEIPHOLZ RETURNS ONE: 1905, entry 1, MARIANNA EMILIA WARGALLA, father Michael, mother GOTTLIEBA LEIPHOLZ, parish RUNOWO KRAJEŃSKIE. That is the province Szubin is in, and the seven spellings this archive had been using would never have reached it.

column1: WARMIŃSKO-MAZURSKIE, births
column2: LEIPHOLZ returns a family: GOTLIB 1781 · DANIEL 1784 · MARIA 1787, all children of GOTLIB (or GOTFRYD) LEIPHOLZ and MARIA KLISS, at ORZYSZ-ARYS (EWANG.), village PIANKI — with a further entry in 1829.

column1: *** AND THIS IS THE WARNING THAT HAS TO GO WITH THE RULE ***
column2: Orzysz is ARYS IN MASURIA, and the register is the PROTESTANT one. An eighteenth-century Lutheran family in Masuria is not a Jewish family from Posen by any reading. SO LEIPHOLZ IS ALSO A GENUINE SURNAME IN ITS OWN RIGHT — German, Protestant, Masurian — QUITE APART FROM BEING THE BERLIN DIRECTORY'S VARIANT OF LEIBHOLZ.

column1: what that means for how the rule is used
column2: the cross-reference proves that SOME Leipholz records belong to Leibholz people — Willi and Jenny settle that. IT DOES NOT PROVE THE REVERSE. Every Leipholz found must still be placed on its own evidence, and the Masurian ones are a separate line that goes on the register as one. THE RULE WIDENS THE SEARCH; IT DOES NOT WIDEN THE FAMILY.

column1: # ---------------- 7. AROLSEN, AND A THIRD PROOF ON A THIRD PERSON ----------------
*** LEIPHOLZ AT AROLSEN: TWO PEOPLE AND THREE T/D CASES ***
column2: the people are "BODIN, ELSE, maiden name LEIPHOLZ, place of birth HAMMERSTEIN, 08/12/1884" and "LEIPHOLZ, HEINZ".

column1: *** AND THE BUNDESARCHIV HAS THE FIRST OF THEM WITH A B ***
column2: the Gedenkbuch's fifty contain "BODIN, ELSE (* 12.08.1884 in HAMMERSTEIN)" — filed under LEIBHOLZ. Same woman, same birth date, same town. A THIRD INSTITUTION, A THIRD PERSON, THE SAME TWO SPELLINGS.

column1: and this one lands on tonight's other finding
column2: Else Bodin was born at HAMMERSTEIN, which is where SALLY LEIBHOLZ was born in 1847 and where five of the Gedenkbuch's fifty were born. The spelling question and the geography question are the same question: THE SURNAME'S HEARTLAND IS KREIS SCHLOCHAU AND ITS CLERKS WROTE IT BOTH WAYS.
